stories.title: SpiceJet cancels flights as board approves fundraise
stories.summary: SpiceJet has cancelled over half its daily flights, leaving thousands stranded. The board has cleared a Rs 5,500-crore fundraise, though executives warn the carrier may shut down if the money does not arrive within a week. The regulator has yet to restrict the airline from taking new bookings.

stories.title: SpiceJet cancels 74 percent of flights at major hubs
stories.summary: SpiceJet cancelled 31 of 42 scheduled flights at Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru airports on Thursday. The cash-strapped carrier is currently cancelling more than half of its daily flights due to unpaid dues and grounded aircraft. The DGCA has issued a show-cause notice to the airline regarding its operations.

stories.title: IndiGo cancels all flights to 4 Saudi cities till Nov 30 amid Houthi attacks - Moneycontrol.com
Air India and IndiGo appoint new CEOs
stories.summary: Air India and IndiGo have hired aviation veterans Tewolde Gebremariam and Willie Walsh to lead their respective airlines. The carriers are undergoing simultaneous resets to manage growth in the Indian market. Both CEOs face the challenge of navigating different business environments at the two largest airlines in the country.

stories.title: Air India Express appoints Deepak Rajawat as CEO
stories.summary: Deepak Rajawat will become the Chief Executive Officer of Air India Express on December 1. Rajawat previously served as the airline's Chief Financial Officer. His stated focus is to create a customer-centric organization that aligns with market needs while navigating challenges in the evolving aviation sector.

stories.title: Centre granted more time for Ahmedabad crash probe
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has granted the Centre two additional weeks to complete the investigation into the June 2025 Ahmedabad plane crash that killed 260 people. The Solicitor General informed the court that the probe is nearing completion. The court is hearing pleas for an independent, monitored investigation.

stories.title: SpiceJet cancellation causes passenger to miss exam
stories.summary: A 21-year-old pilot aspirant missed a DGCA examination after a last-minute SpiceJet cancellation in Mumbai. The passenger alleged that airline staff were unavailable to manage the terminal entrance during the disruption. The flight was rescheduled from 11.55 pm to 2.30 am, according to the airline representative.

stories.title: Noida International Airport begins commercial operations
stories.summary: Noida International Airport has officially opened with an IndiGo flight arriving from Lucknow. Developed by Zurich Airport Limited, the facility is intended to expand air connectivity across the National Capital Region. The airport welcomed its first scheduled flight shortly before 8:00 a.m. on its opening day.

stories.title: Navi Mumbai Airport reaches 3 million passengers
stories.summary: Navi Mumbai International Airport has served 3 million passengers since opening in December 2025. The airport now connects to 46 destinations, up from 13 at launch. It recorded a 94% last-bag delivery performance in August, reflecting a stated focus on baggage handling and passenger operations.

stories.title: Congestion hits Delhi and Mumbai airports
stories.summary: Indian airports handled 420 million passengers in 2025, leading to holding patterns and terminal delays. With IndiGo and Air India ordering over 1,350 new aircraft, the industry is facing a shortage of space to land, park and refuel. The infrastructure is currently struggling to keep pace with growth.

stories.title: Akasa Air adds Chandigarh to network
stories.summary: Akasa Air will launch daily non-stop flights between Chandigarh, Bengaluru and Goa starting December 1. This expansion marks the airline's entry into Punjab and brings its total domestic destinations to 31. The carrier says scaling its presence across India remains central to its long-term growth strategy.

stories.title: IndiGo launches flights from Noida International Airport
stories.summary: IndiGo began commercial operations at the new Noida International Airport in June 2026. The airline is the first to serve the facility and plans to expand to 16 domestic destinations. The airport is the third to open in the National Capital Region, following Delhi and Hindon.

stories.title: Copa Airlines expects 2027 fleet deliveries
stories.summary: Copa Airlines expects to receive 12 Boeing 737-8 aircraft next year. The carrier says it is not concerned that potential delivery delays will impact its 2027 capacity targets. The airline is also retiring two older 737-700 aircraft as part of its fleet management plan for the year.

stories.title: Ibom Air reports annual profit
stories.summary: Nigerian carrier Ibom Air reported a profit of 5.485 billion naira for 2025. Revenue rose 52% to 147.03 billion naira, which the chairman credited to operational discipline and prudent financial management. The airline is currently seeking additional equity investment from its sole shareholder to support its ongoing operations.

stories.title: Philippine Airlines orders 15 Boeing Dreamliners
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines has firmed up an order for 15 Boeing 787-10 aircraft, with an option for five more. The deal, powered by GE Aerospace engines, represents the airline's largest-ever widebody purchase. The agreement marks a milestone in the 80-year partnership between the airline and the manufacturer.

stories.title: Emirates Pushes Airbus to Revive A380 With 100-Jet Order - AirGuide Business
Aer Lingus to introduce premium economy cabins
stories.summary: Aer Lingus will debut premium economy cabins on its long-haul fleet starting October 2027. The airline is refurbishing 10 Airbus A330 aircraft in what it describes as its most significant investment in over a decade. The upgraded planes will serve routes between Dublin and New York.

stories.title: Aer Lingus updates long-haul cabin design
stories.summary: Aer Lingus is refurbishing its Airbus A330 fleet with new business class suites and premium economy cabins. The airline describes the project as its biggest long-haul investment in more than a decade. The redesign aims to elevate the transatlantic passenger experience through a new Irish-inspired design language.

stories.title: Airline Service Quality Performance Data to September 2026 - Bureau of Transportation Statistics (.gov)
Japan and Argentina expand airline operating rights
stories.summary: Japan and Argentina have signed a new aviation framework allowing airlines to operate scheduled passenger and cargo services between the two countries. The agreement permits carriers to serve any airport in either nation, excluding Tokyo Haneda. It does not specify frequencies, intermediate points or fifth-freedom rights.

stories.title: Kuwait signs aviation agreements with UK and Argentina
stories.summary: Kuwait has signed new air transport agreements and memorandums of understanding with the UK and Argentina. The deals were finalized in Montreal during the ICAO Air Transport Conference. The agreements aim to regulate air transport and update frameworks for bilateral cooperation between the nations.

stories.title: Royal Brunei Airlines selects Rolls-Royce for 787 fleet
stories.summary: Royal Brunei Airlines has selected the upgraded Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 XE engine to power four Boeing 787-9 aircraft. The order marks a move by the UK engine maker to rebuild market share on the twinjet. The aircraft were originally ordered in 2024 to augment the existing fleet.

stories.title: Textron to divest Industrials division for $1.2 billion
stories.summary: Textron will sell its Industrials division to Kingwood Capital Management for $1.2 billion. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, with proceeds earmarked for share buybacks and corporate expenses. The company intends to operate exclusively as an aviation and defense firm.

stories.title: Tiberius Aerospace claims unicorn status after funding round
stories.summary: Tiberius Aerospace has raised $85 million in Series A venture capital. The company, which is developing the ramjet-powered Invictus strike missile, now claims a valuation of at least $1 billion. The funding round was led by Lakestar.

stories.title: Cathay Group orders 14 additional Airbus aircraft to expand and modernise fleet - Travel Daily News Asia-Pacific
Hanwha Systems secures US counter-drone radar contract
stories.summary: Hanwha Systems has signed a pilot export contract to supply short-range AESA radars to Rebellion Industries. The deal involves delivering a small number of units to assess suitability for the US market. The companies are currently discussing potential follow-on contracts for larger orders.

stories.title: Gulf Helicopters rebrands to Global Helicopter Company
stories.summary: Doha-based Gulf Helicopters has rebranded as Global Helicopter Company. The rotorcraft operator, one of the largest in the Middle East, announced the change on November 16. The company states the new name is intended to reflect its next phase of growth.

stories.title: Spain faces combat aircraft fleet uncertainty
stories.summary: Spain is approaching snap elections amid a national housing crisis. The incoming government will face a decision regarding the future of the country's combat aircraft fleets. This follows the collapse of the fighter pillar of the trinational Future Combat Air System program.

stories.title: Airbus maritime patrol program faces 65 percent cost increase
stories.summary: A parliamentary report states that costs for the French maritime patrol program, based on the Airbus A321XLR, have risen from 2.76 billion euros to 4.57 billion euros. This 65 percent increase may complicate negotiations with the French defence procurement agency ahead of the planned launch.

stories.title: Airbus maintains 2026 delivery targets
stories.summary: Airbus has reaffirmed its 2026 delivery goal, which requires handing over approximately 250 aircraft in November and December. Commercial division head Lars Wagner stated that all these airframes are currently in final assembly or on delivery lines. Final assembly is not the same as a completed handover.

stories.title: Airbus relies on final assembly for year-end targets
stories.summary: Airbus aims to hand over 250 aircraft in the final two months of 2026 to meet its annual target. Lars Wagner, head of the commercial business, confirmed all units are in final assembly or on delivery lines. The plan places factory floors under significant scrutiny.

stories.title: FAA oversight questioned following nationwide ground stop
stories.summary: Reports indicate the FAA maintained limited oversight of the work that preceded a recent nationwide ground stop. The incident occurred alongside other technical disruptions across various sectors. The agency has not provided further details regarding the specific oversight failures.

stories.title: FAA account attributes ground stop to cutover error
stories.summary: An FAA account suggests the recent ground stop resulted from a cutover error rather than equipment failure. The incident follows a similar 2009 event where construction damage to a telecommunications cabinet disabled radar and radio services, forcing controllers to coordinate traffic using backup handheld radios.

stories.title: FAA stopped its system from crashing. But has it fixed what caused the ground stop? - Cleveland.com
USDOT requests $50.1 billion for air traffic modernization
stories.summary: The Trump Administration has asked Congress to fund a 50.1 billion dollar modernization of the air traffic control system. The proposal follows a four-hour ground stop attributed to a router upgrade. The administration is calling for the implementation of a new system to prevent future outages.

stories.title: US plans to announce cause of outage that led to nationwide ground stop, FAA says - Reuters
Ground Stop Came as Duffy Pushed to Rapidly Upgrade Aviation Systems - The New York Times
‘Blame me’: FAA chief takes fall for nationwide flight grounding - Politico
FAA ground stop highlights aging infrastructure
stories.summary: A single router failure in the Federal Aviation Administration’s telecommunications network caused a nationwide ground stop on November 13, resulting in 18,000 cancellations. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy blamed the agency’s incredibly old telecommunication system. The agency is now scrambling to identify the precise cause of the failure.

stories.title: Congress reaches aviation safety agreement
stories.summary: House and Senate leaders have agreed on aviation safety legislation addressing National Transportation Safety Board recommendations. The deal focuses on Automatic Dependent Surveillance to Broadcast systems that operate without pilot or controller input. The agreement follows a 2025 midair collision between a commercial jet and an Army helicopter.

stories.title: DGCA proposes separate aircraft registration system
stories.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation has proposed a dedicated registration mechanism for prototype and production testing. The plan allows manufacturers to obtain test flight marks without using the regular civil aircraft register. The proposal also seeks to tighten documentation requirements for aircraft taken on dry lease.

stories.title: India expands pilot training capacity
stories.summary: The government has awarded Letters of Intent for 11 new Flying Training Organisations across seven airports. Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu also launched an app to streamline instrument flight training. The expansion is expected to increase annual training capacity by 750 cadets.

stories.title: Bell opens Oklahoma helicopter training facility
stories.summary: Semper Fly Helicopters is now offering Bell-approved training for the Bell 206 at its Norman facility. The school operates under FAR Part 141 or 61. Bell Training Academy general manager Chad Sparks stated the goal is to develop a challenging and accessible program for new pilots.

stories.title: FAA reports Vets2Wings program outcomes
stories.summary: The FAA reports that its Vets2Wings program has produced 39 graduates and currently supports 66 active students. Since 2022, participants have obtained 192 pilot certificates and ratings. The initiative provides financial and career support to military veterans pursuing civilian pilot qualifications in partnership with the University of North Dakota.

stories.title: Apex Aviation plans Texas flight school
stories.summary: Startup Apex Aviation Training Group is developing a flight school for the Austin area with a 2027 launch target. The company has drafted curricula for private, instrument, and commercial pilot qualifications. Operations remain subject to securing aircraft, a physical location, and the necessary arrangements for flight instruction.

stories.title: UND joins NOAA aviation partnership
stories.summary: The University of North Dakota is one of three universities selected to establish a Cooperative Aviation Center with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The partnership creates a career pathway for students to fly scientific research aircraft, including those used for hurricane reconnaissance and atmospheric studies.

stories.title: K-State Salina named NOAA aviation partner
stories.summary: Kansas State University Salina has been selected as an inaugural National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Cooperative Aviation Center. The program, based on 2020 legislation, aims to create a pipeline of qualified pilots for the federal agency. K-State Salina joins two other universities in the partnership.

stories.title: KSU Salina joins NOAA pilot pipeline
stories.summary: Kansas State University Salina will host a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Cooperative Aviation Center to feed student pilots into the NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps. The center is designed to address a shortage of specialized pilots. It joins programs at the Florida Institute of Technology and North Dakota.

stories.title: Paragon Flight gains check ride authority
stories.summary: Paragon Flight Training has received FAA authorization to conduct practical tests for its own students. The academy plans to eventually offer testing to applicants from other schools to address Designated Pilot Examiner shortages. The company says access to check rides has been a significant frustration for years.

stories.title: FAA accepts updated aircraft certification standards
stories.summary: The FAA has accepted ASTM F3264-25 as a means of compliance for 65 sections of Part 23 aircraft certification. The standards cover flight characteristics, structural strength, and electrical systems. The updated provisions include new requirements for demonstrating acceptable stall and low-speed handling characteristics for aircraft design.

stories.title: Pakistan cancels pilot licenses following probe
stories.summary: Pakistan has canceled 50 pilot licenses and suspended 33 others following allegations of fraud. The Ministry of Defence confirmed the action was taken under Civil Aviation Rules. Previous fake license allegations led to international flight restrictions that cost Pakistan International Airlines an estimated PKR 200 billion in revenue.

research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The effect of aiding buoyancy on flow past a square cylinder has previously been shown to suppress vortex shedding above a critical Richardson number (Ri), transitioning from unsteady to steady flow. Building on this, the present. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Comparison of Open-Source PSCAD EMT Models for Large-Scale AI Data Centers in Smart Grids
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid deployment of artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs) introduces gigawatt-scale, highly nonlinear, and fast-varying electronic loads that challenge grid voltage regulation, frequency stability, and disturbance ride-through. Capturing their transient behavior during grid faults and rapid. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part I: The gravity force term
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The OpenFOAM solver interFoam for incompressible two-phase flows combines the single-phase PISO/PIMPLE algorithm for the pressure-velocity coupling with an interface advection step. It relies on the standard finite volume discretisation of the momentum equation, which assumes. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part II: The momentum convection term
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The two-phase Volume-of-Fluid solvers of OpenFOAM overpredict the horizontal water velocity near the crest of a water wave, and the error grows as the wave propagates. Part I of this series removed the spurious air velocities. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Construction of a Deployable Hard-Constrained Turbulence Closure
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a framework for constructing deployable hard-constrained turbulence closures of unclosed terms in the transport equations of Reynolds stresses and turbulent dissipation rate. The framework is built from modules, each performing a single task. The. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Control-Aware Separating Hyperplanes for Control Barrier Functions in Planar Navigation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Separating hyperplanes are widely used in Control Barrier Function (CBF)-based collision avoidance, yet their orientations strongly govern control intervention-the deviation of the applied control from the robot's nominal command. Existing methods typically select hyperplane orientations from. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Data-Driven Factored Abstractions of Stochastic Systems
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Formal verification and correct-by-design policy synthesis for stochastic dynamical systems face significant scalability challenges due to the curse of dimensionality. These challenges are exacerbated when the system dynamics are unknown and abstractions must be constructed from. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Data-driven control of polynomial systems using implicit methods
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: While conventional behavioral data-driven control represents linear time-invariant (LTI) systems directly from data, extending these data representations to nonlinear systems remains an open challenge. We address this gap for general polynomial systems, characterizing their finite-length trajectories. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
